# gh-1403: [feat] reviewPolicy.verification: none | filter — a finding-filter leg before posting (ByteDance ReviewFilter pattern)

## Description

## Problem

The review leg is built for maximal recall, and every rework-tier finding arms a rework lap (15–20 CI min + quota). Wrong or speculative findings cost laps exactly like real ones — the only verification today is the reviewer's own prose. Measured on PR #1387: ~8–9 machine comments per rework lap, ~1 with decision value.

We want a second stage that **verifies findings before they cost a lap**, configurable so owners choose whether to pay for it.

## The approach: a filter leg (ByteDance BitsAI-CR pattern)

ByteDance runs exactly this in production at 12k+ WAU: a recall stage generates candidates, a separate **ReviewFilter** pass verifies each against the code — 75% precision, and their precision KPI ("Outdated Rate" = share of flagged lines developers actually changed) is computed from outcomes, not opinions.

- Research: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15134 (BitsAI-CR: Automated Code Review via LLM in Practice)

**Why filter (and not alternatives):**
- Proven at scale, only ~1× extra review cost per round.
- A fresh context optimizes precision and never self-justifies the finder's claims (self-preference bias is a documented LLM-judge failure mode).
- An "evidence rule" (findings must cite input X → line Y → Z) was rejected for v1: it fits correctness claims but ⚠️/architecture findings are judgment calls — there is no failing scenario for "this coupling is wrong"; forced evidence shape = gaming or wholesale demotion.
- Majority voting is deferred — same idea at ×N cost, trivially addable later.

## How it should work

- Config: `reviewPolicy.verification = none | filter` (default `none` — owners opt in). Voting may land later as `filter` with N passes.
- **This repository is the trial subject**: dmtools-agents ships `reviewPolicy.verification` but MERGES WITH `'none'` (human decision 2026-11-09 — merging with `'filter'` active crashes review legs against pre-gh-1403 packs, observed live on #1407's review run); the opt-in to `'filter'` flips right after merge in #1408, so this repo's own laps (see #1387, #1392) are the baseline and the trial data in one place.
- **Placement**: after the review leg produces `outputs/pr_review.json`, before posting (postPRReviewComments step 4). A `filter` flag on `pr_review.json` or a sibling `pr_review_filter.json` leg.
- **Input**: candidate findings + the diff hunks + the interaction neighborhood (callers/callees of changed symbols — not whole files; over-broad context manufactures findings). The filter does **not** see the finder's severity or rationale (anchoring/self-preference guard).
- **Output per candidate**: `keep | demote(<tier>) | drop` + one-line reason.
- **Machine semantics**: census is recomputed **after** filtering (gh-1351 machinery untouched). `drop` → digest-only line (visible, never a thread); `demote` → tier downgrade. Only rework/polish-tier candidates are filtered; 💡-digest/🪶 never go through.
- **Anti-over-suppression**: drop-rate logged per round; dropped candidates listed in the general comment / escalation packet (one line each). Drop-rate ≈ 100% = misconfigured filter, not a better reviewer.

## Trial (before promoting beyond opt-in)

Dogfood on this repository (its own PRs — incl. factory-bot PRs — are reviewed by the same machinery), plus the separate test repo if more volume is needed. Measure:
1. rework laps per PR vs baseline,
2. precision = kept findings that led to a fix ÷ kept total (Outdated-Rate style, computed from gh-1332 dispositions we already collect),
3. wrongly-dropped real issues (owner spot-audit of the dropped list).

Success bar: laps/PR ↓ AND precision ↑ AND wrongly-dropped ≈ 0.

## Out of scope
- Review-prompt decision-rule rewrite — IstiN/dmtools-agents#1404 (prompt edits need their own careful change per research: detail-rich prompts measurably amplify over-reporting; and shipping both together makes trial attribution impossible).
- Polish laps — untouched until cost/Outdated-Rate data exists.
- Cross-model verification (a different model for the filter pass) — v1 runs the filter on the SAME model as the finder; `AI_REVIEW_FILTER_MODEL` was dropped from the implementation (human decision 2026-11-09, #1407 795b9ba). Revisit after trial data.
- Lessons/feedback loop, majority voting — later.

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-story-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/42592796491) · started 09:22 · done 10:13 ✅
- [x] ▶ review (fa-review) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/42599690094) · started 10:17 · done 10:17 ✅



## Human decisions (2026-11-09)
- **Same-model v1**: `AI_REVIEW_FILTER_MODEL` removed from issue scope, PR #1407 (795b9ba) and the deployment plan — the filter runs on the finder's model until trial data justifies cross-model cost. Note: dev legs ingest `title` + `body` of the assigned issue only (no comments), so this body is the machine-legible spec.
- **No `reviewPolicy` block at merge, opt-in added via #1408**: the block (even with `'none'`) crashes released packs' leg setup on this checkout — review and rework laps died before any agent booted (bootstrap deadlock, live 2026-11-09). #1407 ships the knob blockless; #1408 adds the `'filter'` opt-in as the very next queued item once a pack release cut from post-gh-1403 main is out.
- The 10:17 review run ✅ in the checklist above is a mark-job-done artifact — the run actually FAILED (old pack rejected `verification`; no verdict, gh-305 diagnosis posted). CI is red on record; the PR is human-revised instead of reworked.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1407 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1407 - **Title**: gh-1403 [feat] reviewPolicy.verification: none filter — a finding-filter leg before posting (ByteDance ReviewFilter pattern) - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1403` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 13 - **Additions**: +2346 - **Deletions**: -218 - **Created**: 2026-11-09T10:13:26Z - **Updated**: 2026-11-09T12:22:43Z ## PR Description Closes #1403 ### Human revision (2026-11-09, 795b9ba) - `AI_REVIEW_FILTER_MODEL` dropped — the verification pass runs on the **same model as the finder** in v1 (cross-model deliberately deferred; tracked in #1408 Out of scope). # pr review

Reviews a pull request like a senior reviewer: analyzes the diff, checks conventions and risks, and posts inline review comments plus a verdict.

## Parameters

Configured via `customParams` in the agent JSON or the project `.dmtools/config.js` (project values win).

- `cacheToReleases` — when enabled, the autocommit timer snapshots accumulated CLI output into a git release asset.
- `scmProvider` — SCM provider override (`github`, `gitlab`, …) for this run.
- `targetRepository` — repository override block (`owner`, `repo`, `baseBranch`, `workingDir`) — run the review against this repository instead of the project default.

- `aiRepository` — repository the AI CLI works in when it differs from the PR repository.
- `allowApproveWithSuggestions` — legacy knob (gh-1351): policy-derived now; setting it against the resolved `reviewPolicy` logs a conflict audit line and the policy wins.
- `autoStartRework` — when `true`, automatically trigger the rework workflow when the review asks for changes.
- `autoStartReworkConfigFile` — agent config file used for the auto-started rework workflow.
- `checkOpenPR` — when `true`, skip tickets that already have an open pull request for this work.
- `configPath` — path to the project `.dmtools/config.js` to load for this run.
- `customStatuses` — legacy per-invocation override for individual `STATUSES` keys (e.g. `{ "IN_REWORK": "Ready For Development" }`); prefer the project-wide `jira.statuses` override in `.dmtools/config.js` for a project-wide remap instead.
- `formalGithubReview` — when `true`, in addition to the existing `pr_approved` label, formally submit a native GitHub PR review: `REQUEST_CHANGES` when the AI does not approve, or dismiss any prior `REQUEST_CHANGES` review when the AI approves. Does not change the `pr_approved` label lifecycle.
- `maxAutoReworkRounds` — maximum auto-started rework rounds (`rework-round-N` on the ticket, default `3`; values `<= 0` warn and fall back to `3` — use `autoStartRework: false` to disable) before the ticket is labeled `needs-human` and no further rework is chained.
- `maxReviewThreadsBeforeForceApprove` — maximum open review threads before the reviewer is forced to an approve/reject verdict.
- `onApproved` — action to run when the review approves (e.g. trigger merge).
- `projectKey` — tracker project key override.
- `removeLabel` — label removed from the ticket after a successful run (idempotency cleanup).

## Review policy: `reviewPolicy.verification` (gh-1403)

Set in the project `.dmtools/config.js` (e.g. `reviewPolicy: { verification: 'filter' }`); jobParams `reviewPolicy` overrides per run. The resolved table stamped into `review_policy.md` documents the active value.

- `none` (default) — findings post exactly as the review leg raised them. No extra cost, no extra risk.
- `filter` — a second, FRESH-context CLI pass re-verifies each file-referenced finding against the actual PR diff before it is posted, and rewrites the review:
  - `demote` — a still-valid finding loses its tier (no longer gates approval), its body is kept and prefixed with the machine-parsed provenance marker `dmtools:demoted-from-BLOCKING` / `dmtools:demoted-from-IMPORTANT`, the thread is resolved.
  - `drop` — a non-finding is removed, its thread resolved.
  - `keep` (default) — the finding posts unchanged. Round-none tiers (🪶 under the default preset) never enter the filter.
  - Anti-over-suppression guard: when every candidate of a run is dropped/demoted and kept ≪ candidates, a ⚠️ warning is stamped into the review summary — a miscalibrated filter must not silently erase real findings.

**Trial opt-in** (gh-1403): this repository itself opts in via `.dmtools/config.js`; the trial bar is fewer rework laps per PR AND higher precision AND ≈ 0 wrongly-dropped findings. Revert to `none` if the trial fails.

# Pr Review

Reviews a pull request like a senior reviewer: analyzes the diff, checks conventions and risks, and posts inline review comments plus a verdict.

## Parameters

Configured via `customParams` in the agent JSON or the project `.dmtools/config.js` (project values win).

- `cacheToReleases` — when enabled, the autocommit timer snapshots accumulated CLI output into a git release asset.
- `scmProvider` — SCM provider override (`github`, `gitlab`, …) for this run.
- `targetRepository` — repository override block (`owner`, `repo`, `baseBranch`, `workingDir`) — run the review against this repository instead of the project default.

- `aiRepository` — repository the AI CLI works in when it differs from the PR repository.
- `allowApproveWithSuggestions` — legacy knob (gh-1351): policy-derived now; setting it against the resolved `reviewPolicy` logs a conflict audit line and the policy wins.
- `autoStartRework` — when `true`, automatically trigger the rework workflow when the review asks for changes.
- `autoStartReworkConfigFile` — agent config file used for the auto-started rework workflow.
- `checkOpenPR` — when `true`, skip tickets that already have an open pull request for this work.
- `configPath` — path to the project `.dmtools/config.js` to load for this run.
- `customStatuses` — legacy per-invocation override for individual `STATUSES` keys (e.g. `{ "IN_REWORK": "Ready For Development" }`); prefer the project-wide `jira.statuses` override in `.dmtools/config.js` for a project-wide remap instead.
- `formalGithubReview` — when `true`, in addition to the existing `pr_approved` label, formally submit a native GitHub PR review: `REQUEST_CHANGES` when the AI does not approve, or dismiss any prior `REQUEST_CHANGES` review when the AI approves. Does not change the `pr_approved` label lifecycle.
- `maxAutoReworkRounds` — maximum auto-started rework rounds (`rework-round-N` on the ticket, default `3`; values `<= 0` warn and fall back to `3` — use `autoStartRework: false` to disable) before the ticket is labeled `needs-human` and no further rework is chained.
- `maxReviewThreadsBeforeForceApprove` — maximum open review threads before the reviewer is forced to an approve/reject verdict.
- `onApproved` — action to run when the review approves (e.g. trigger merge).
- `projectKey` — tracker project key override.
- `removeLabel` — label removed from the ticket after a successful run (idempotency cleanup).

## Review policy: `reviewPolicy.verification` (gh-1403)

Set in the project `.dmtools/config.js` (e.g. `reviewPolicy: { verification: 'filter' }`); jobParams `reviewPolicy` overrides per run. The resolved table stamped into `review_policy.md` documents the active value.

content.text:
----
Example PR review outputs — keep concise:

### outputs/pr_review.json
```json
{
  "recommendation": "BLOCK",
  "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.",
  "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md",
  "inlineComments": [
    {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"},
    {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"},
    {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"},
    {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":20,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md","severity":"NIT"}
  ],
  "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1,"nits":1}
}
```

**Severity boundary (gh-1351, 4 tiers)**: a 🪶 NIT changes nothing behavioral and
nothing documented (style, naming, formatting, micro-symmetry); a 💡 SUGGESTION
changes clarity of the documented/behavioral surface (missing docs, unclear
contract, better API shape). Anything that changes behavior or breaks a
documented contract is ⚠️ IMPORTANT or 🚨 BLOCKING.

### outputs/pr_review_general.md
```markdown
## Automated Code Review — BLOCK

**Summary**: SQL injection blocks merge. One important issue (weak password validation) and one suggestion (extract duplicated validation).

**Next Steps**:
1. Fix SQL injection in UserService.js — use parameterized queries
2. Strengthen password validation (8+ chars, mixed case, numbers, symbols)
3. Extract shared email validation utility
```

### outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md
```markdown
🚨 **BLOCKING: SQL Injection**

User input is interpolated directly into the query at `UserService.js:45`:

```javascript
const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`;
```

Use parameterized queries instead:

```javascript
const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?';
await db.query(query, [email]);
```
```

Set in the project `.dmtools/config.js` (e.g. `reviewPolicy: { verification: 'filter' }`); jobParams `reviewPolicy` overrides per run. The resolved table stamped into `review_policy.md` documents the active value.

- `none` (default) — findings post exactly as the review leg raised them. No extra cost, no extra risk.
- `filter` — a second, FRESH-context CLI pass re-verifies each file-referenced finding against the actual PR diff before it is posted, and rewrites the review:
  - `demote` — a still-valid finding loses its tier (no longer gates approval), its body is kept and prefixed with the machine-parsed provenance marker `dmtools:demoted-from-BLOCKING` / `dmtools:demoted-from-IMPORTANT`, the thread is resolved.
  - `drop` — a non-finding is removed, its thread resolved.
  - `keep` (default) — the finding posts unchanged. Round-none tiers (🪶 under the default preset) never enter the filter.
  - Anti-over-suppression guard: when every candidate of a run is dropped or demoted (nothing kept — a fully-demoted round flips every gated finding to non-gating too), a ⚠️ warning is stamped into the review summary — a miscalibrated filter must not silently erase real findings.

**Trial opt-in** (gh-1403): this repository itself opts in via `.dmtools/config.js`; the trial bar is fewer rework laps per PR AND higher precision AND ≈ 0 wrongly-dropped findings. Revert to `none` if the trial fails.

arguments.content:
**Fixed.** The demote stamp no longer writes to `entry.comment` unguarded — the model-written path now passes through the same shape guard every other model-written file reference in this module applies.

- `js/postPRReviewComments.js` — extracted the shared guard `isCommentFilePath(value)` (the exact `^(outputs\/)?(pr_review_comments\/)?[\w.\-]+\.md$` shape `resolveCommentFileReference` used inline) and applied it to **all three** call sites: `resolveCommentFileReference` (read), `filterPathOfGeneralComment` (write), and now `stampOneDemotion` (write). A hallucinated/nested/foreign `comment` value (`docs/agents/pr_review.md`, `sub/dir/note.md`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`) can no longer be read-then-appended by the demote stamp — the stamp is skipped and the demote still applies to the structured severity.
- Regression tests (`js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js`): "stampOneDemotion — a non-comment-file path is never written (gh-1350 class guard)" — a demote on an entry whose `comment` points at a readable repo doc writes nothing; and "stampOneDemotion — hostile model-written shapes are refused" (nested dir, workflow YAML). Both reproduce the reported shape against the pre-fix code (verified RED before the fix).
- Verified: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_postPRReviewComments.json` — 194 passed, 0 failed (full `run_all` green on the rework head).

Fixed in commit `<SHA>`.

**Fixed** (your first suggested option — reconcile, no BLOCKING carve-out). A surviving `BLOCK`/`REQUEST_CHANGES` token is now advisory when the filter applied changes and the post-filter census gates nothing: the machine verdict follows the census, exactly the way gh-1351 treats an `APPROVE` token.

- `js/postPRReviewComments.js` — new `reconcileFilterTokenWithCensus(machine, filterOutcome, issueCounts, policy)`, applied in `action()` right after `machineApprovalFromCensus`: when `filterOutcome` exists (the filter leg applied ≥ 1 verdict) and `reviewPolicyModule.hasBlockingOrImportant(...)` is false, a non-approve machine verdict is replaced by `{ approved: true, verdict: 'APPROVE', recomputed: true }` — which flows through the existing `buildMachineVerdictLog` line, so the reconciliation is logged (`advisory BLOCK → effective APPROVE — filter applied (gh-1403): post-filter census has no rework-tier threads`).
- The invariants you called out are preserved and pinned by tests: **without an applied filter, `BLOCK` stands untouched** (`machineApprovalDecision`'s short-circuit is not overridden — "action() — a BLOCK token stands when no filter ran (verification none keeps the invariant)"), and **a filter round that leaves a BLOCKING thread posted keeps the non-approve verdict** ("action() — a BLOCK token stands when the post-filter census still gates"). The wasted-lap scenario you described (BLOCK + `issueCounts.blocking = 0` + zero blocking threads → rework lap armed) now resolves to APPROVE with the digest lines still listing every drop.
- Tests: `js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js` — 3 new action()-level tests (RED-verified against the pre-fix code). Full `run_all` green on the rework head.

Fixed in commit `<SHA>`.

**Fixed.** The anchoring guard now also strips the prose severity header form.

- `js/common/reviewFilter.js` — `claimOf` applies a second strip after `reviewVerdicts.stripLeadingSeverityLine`: `stripProseSeverityHead` removes the first line when it heads with a tier word (`BLOCKING|IMPORTANT|SUGGESTION|NIT`, case-insensitive — the `EXPLICIT_SEVERITY_RE` vocabulary), with the tier emoji and `**` bold markers optional and a colon required: the exact few-shots shape `🚨 **BLOCKING: SQL Injection**` and its unembellished `**BLOCKING: …**` variant. The whole header line (title included) drops — that line is severity classification; the claim's substance starts below it. Head-of-claim only: a tier word further down the claim ("this helper is important for the parser contract") is data, not protocol, and is pinned untouched by test.
- Pinned with the few-shots body shape as requested: `js/unit-tests/test_reviewFilter.js` — "the claim is severity-stripped in the few-shots prose form too (🚨 **BLOCKING: title**)" (RED-verified against the pre-fix code) plus a per-tier-words sweep and the mid-claim control. `pr_review_filter_input.json` no longer carries the finder's classification in either form.
- Verified: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_reviewFilter.json` — 50 passed, 0 failed (full `run_all` green on the rework head).

Fixed in commit `<SHA>`.

**Fixed** (your second option — the code now matches the docs, not the other way around). `buildOverSuppressionWarning` fires whenever every candidate of a round was suppressed with **nothing kept** — `dropped + demoted === candidates` — so a fully-demoted round (4/4 demoted, 0 dropped) warns exactly like a full-drop round.

- `js/common/reviewFilter.js` — the trigger moved from `stats.dropped < stats.candidates → null` to: `kept > 0 → null`, then `demoted + dropped < candidates → null`. The warning message now names both counts ("N/M dropped, K demoted — every candidate of the run was suppressed (0 kept)"), and the module header + `docs/agents/pr_review.md` were aligned with the implemented trigger (the generated copy `docs/agents/generated/pr_review.md` regenerated via `node js/agentDocGenerator.js`). Your caution is folded into both: a fully-demoted round flips every gated finding to non-gating, so it earns the same "silence is not precision" scrutiny — that is why it warns.
- Tests (`js/unit-tests/test_reviewFilter.js`): all-demoted warns, mixed demote/drop with 0 kept warns, any round with ≥ 1 kept stays silent, full-drop still warns (existing pin unchanged). RED-verified against the pre-fix code.

- **CI**: no owned violations — `ci_failures.md` reports all checks green on the rework head; no "Violations you must fix" table. No CI root cause to chase.

The stale "How to verify" test counts in the **PR description** (31/31/180 → actual 40/74/185, grown further this lap) live on GitHub, not in the repo — not fixable from this branch; re-run the three `dmtools run` commands below for current counts.
- No downgrades: all three ⚠️ findings were real and were fixed in code; nothing was demoted to 💡.

## Approach

TDD per finding (RED first — every new test was verified failing against the pre-fix code, then GREEN):

1. **⚠️ `filterDiffPathOf` diff-path derivation** — now walks `ticketKeyShapes.inputFolderCandidates(inputFolderPath, ticketKey)` and probes for the first candidate holding `pr_diff.txt` (the `readTicketClaimSource` pattern), unwrapping the `jobParams`-wrapped params shape (`linkedIssuesReport.resolveInputContext` style). Composite key `owner/repo#1407` → `input/gh-1407/pr_diff.txt`; sanitized keys resolve their derived folder; no candidate holding the file degrades to naming the first candidate (fail-open).
2. **⚠️ `stampOneDemotion` unguarded write** — extracted the shared `isCommentFilePath(value)` guard (the `resolveCommentFileReference` shape) and applied it to all three model-written-path call sites: `resolveCommentFileReference` (read), `filterPathOfGeneralComment` (write), `stampOneDemotion` (write). A hallucinated `comment` value can no longer redirect a demote-stamp append onto any readable repo file.
3. **⚠️ `BLOCK` token surviving the filter** — new `reconcileFilterTokenWithCensus(...)` in the wired leg: when the filter applied changes and the post-filter census gates nothing, a surviving `BLOCK`/`REQUEST_CHANGES` token is advisory (gh-1351 `APPROVE`-token treatment) — the machine verdict follows the census and is logged through the standard machine-enforcement line. Invariants preserved and pinned: without an applied filter `BLOCK` stands untouched; a kept BLOCKING thread keeps the non-approve verdict.
4. **💡 anchoring guard prose leak** — `claimOf` now also strips the prose severity header (`🚨 **BLOCKING: SQL Injection**`, emoji/bold optional, tier-word vocabulary, head-of-claim line only); pinned with the few-shots body shape plus a mid-claim control ("this helper is important…" is data, never stripped).
5. **💡 over-suppression trigger** — took the code option: `buildOverSuppressionWarning` fires when every candidate was dropped **or demoted** with 0 kept (`demoted + dropped === candidates`), message names both counts; docs (`docs/agents/pr_review.md`) aligned with the implemented trigger and the generated copy regenerated (`node js/agentDocGenerator.js`); a fully-demoted round now earns the same "silence is not precision" warning as a full-drop round.
6. **🪶 `run_all.json` re-sort** — intentional normalization, no code change; replied with the rationale (reply-only thread; the reviewer's own bar "if intentional, fine" is met, and future PRs will split such normalization into a dedicated `chore:` commit).

### 1. `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs61Q7UP` — **unknown** (`js/postPRReviewComments.js:1243`)

⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the demote provenance note misses two tolerated input shapes — the note is lost, or the posted thread is corrupted**

The demote path delivers its provenance note through two mechanisms, and both have gaps against the input shapes the poster explicitly tolerates ("Accept both spec formats: old spec `{ file, comment }`, agent output `{ path, body }"` — `postInlineComment`). Verified against this branch's code with a live reproduction (`reviewFilter.applyFilterVerdicts` + the exported `isCommentFilePath`):

**Shape A — body-as-path hybrid → corrupted posted thread.** `stampDemotionBody` (js/common/reviewFilter.js:341-345) appends the note to `entry.body` whenever it is a non-empty string. For the shape `resolveInlineComment` exists for — `body` holding the comment-file *path* — the append turns the path into `outputs/pr_review_comments/c1.md\n---\n⚠️ **Severity demoted: …**`. At post time `isCommentFilePath` no longer matches (the string now contains a newline), so the poster publishes the **literal path + note instead of the claim content** — the finding's substance disappears from the thread. Reproduced:

```javascript
body before: "outputs/pr_review_comments/c1.md"
body after demote: "outputs/pr_review_comments/c1.md\n---\n⚠️ **Severity demoted: review-filter demotion (gh-1403)** — fresh-context verification: overstated"
isCommentFilePath(body after) → false  // poster posts it literally
```

`stampOneDemotion` then also appends the note to the comment file — double provenance, and the posted text still never shows the claim.

**Shape B — old-spec `{file, comment}` → note silently missing.** `filterCandidateOf` reads `c.path || c.file || ''` (js/common/reviewFilter.js:126), so the candidate carries `path: 'a.js'`, but the stamp targeting compares `entry.path` only (`isStampTarget`, js/postPRReviewComments.js:1243-1246): `entry.path` is `undefined` for old-spec entries → no match → the demotion note never lands in the comment file. The structured severity *is* downgraded (the machine-stamped severity line is correct), but the documented contract — "its body is kept and prefixed with the machine-parsed provenance marker" (docs/agents/pr_review.md:34) — silently doesn't hold, and the gh-1332 registry loses the demotion marker it cuts claims at.

Not reachable under the merge-time default `verification: 'none'`; reachable once #1408 flips the knob. Same reachability profile as the F3 fix from the last lap.

**Suggestion**: make the demote-note delivery shape-aware — (1) in `stampDemotionBody`, skip bodies that pass `isCommentFilePath` (let `stampOneDemotion` stamp the file, or resolve the file content into `body` first); (2) in `isStampTarget`, compare `(entry.path || entry.file)` against `stamp.path`. Pin both with tests using the two tolerated shapes.

### 6. `pr_discussions.md:dmtools-factory-bot[bot]:2026-11-09:01e2183d` — **dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-11-09

⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `stampOneDemotion` writes to `entry.comment` without the path-shape guard every other model-written file reference applies**

```javascript
function stampOneDemotion(entry, stamp, ctx) {
    entry.__filterNoted = true;
    if (!entry.comment) return;
    var content = readMarkdownFile(entry.comment, ctx.ticketKey, ctx.workingDir);

```

`entry.comment` comes from the review agent's `outputs/pr_review.json` — a model-written field. This file already treats model-written file references as untrusted input:

- `resolveCommentFileReference` (line 222) gates reads behind `/^(outputs\/)?(pr_review_comments\/)?[\w.\-]+\.md$/`.
- `filterPathOfGeneralComment` (line ~1150, this PR) applies the same regex before `appendDroppedSection` writes.

The demote stamp is the one new write path that skips the guard. The `if (content)` read-before-write narrows the blast radius (the target must have been readable), but a malformed/hallucinated `comment` value still lets a demote **append to (i.e. modify) any readable file relative to the runtime cwd** — e.g. a repo source file or a workflow YAML — instead of the intended `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md`. gh-1350 was introduced for exactly this class ("observed in production": model-written shapes going wrong).

**Suggestion**: reuse the `resolveCommentFileReference`-style regex here (or extract it into a shared `isCommentFilePath(value)` helper and apply it to both call sites) so every model-written path write is guarded identically.

The new leg allows `drop`/`demote` on **BLOCKING** candidates (rework tier → filterable), and the census is correctly recomputed post-filter. But the verdict re-derivation does not fully follow:

1. The review leg emits `recommendation: 'BLOCK'` (security/data-loss token) plus its supporting BLOCKING finding(s).
2. The filter drops all rework-tier candidates → `recomputeCensus` yields `blocking: 0` (dropped candidates become digest lines) — the posted evidence no longer contains any blocking thread.
3. `machineApprovalDecision` (js/common/reviewPolicy.js:427-429) short-circuits: `if (raw === 'BLOCK') return { approved: false, verdict: 'BLOCK', reason: 'model BLOCK (security/data-loss) stands' }` — the pre-filter token outranks the post-filter census.
4. `censusCrossCheckOverride` only corrects the **APPROVE** direction (posted BLOCKING severity + approving verdict), so nothing reconciles a non-approve verdict against a clean census.

Result: the PR is posted as `BLOCK` with `issueCounts.blocking = 0` and no blocking thread on it, and a rework lap is armed for findings the machine itself just declared non-findings — the exact wasted-lap cost gh-1403 exists to remove.

Not reachable under the merge-time default `verification: 'none'`; reachable once #1408 flips the knob.

**Suggestion**: when the filter applied changes and the post-filter census has no rework-tier threads left, treat a surviving `BLOCK`/`REQUEST_CHANGES` token as advisory the same way gh-1351 treats an `APPROVE` token (log the reconciliation; the machine verdict follows the census). Alternatively, exclude BLOCKING candidates from filterable tiers if "model BLOCK always stands" is the intended invariant — but then the docs should say so, since the PR description states drops apply to "each rework/polish-tier finding" with no BLOCKING carve-out.

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read the contents of a text file or image. Text output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large text files. Images are returned as base64 content. Video files route to a video-capable model when one is available (the bytes are attached or described with attribution); otherwise a note names how to configure video reading.

## Path selectors

Append a trailing selector to `path` to read exactly the lines you need:

- `:N` — start at line N (1-indexed), through end of file. `:N-` is the same.
- `:A-B` — inclusive line range (`:A..B` works too).
- `:A+C` — C lines starting at A.
- `:R1,R2,…` — multiple ranges, sorted and merged (`:5-16,960-973`); blocks are joined with a `…` separator and ranges past end of file are reported as skipped.
- `:raw` — verbatim content: no line numbers, no hashline header, no notices. Combine as `:raw:50-100` or `:50-100:raw`.

Do not combine `offset`/`limit` with a path selector. Selectors only apply to text files (not images).

## Archives

Read inside `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`/`.tgz` files: `archive.zip` lists the root, `archive.zip:dir/` lists a directory, `archive.zip:inner/file.txt` reads a member (selectors apply, e.g. `archive.zip:inner/file.txt:50-60`). Binary members return a note.

## SQLite databases

When the host supports it, `.db`/`.db3`/`.sqlite`/`.sqlite3` paths read as databases: `data.db` lists tables, `data.db:table` shows the schema plus sample rows, `data.db:table:key` fetches one row by primary key (or rowid), `data.db:table?limit=20&offset=40&order=col:desc&where=...` pages a table, and `data.db?q=SELECT ...` runs a raw read-only query.

## Hashline mode

Set hashline=true to prefix lines with line numbers and a [path#TAG] content-hash header for anchoring hashline edit patches (line numbers stay correct on ranged reads). Suppressed by `:raw`.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file, creating parent directories as needed. Overwrites the file if it already exists.

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,
# but you replace 2.=4, retype the keepers, and risk dropping one.
SWAP 2.=4:
+    msg = "Hello, " + name
+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)
# RIGHT — touch nothing you keep; the new line is the whole body.
INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)
</anti-patterns>

<critical>
If you remember nothing else:
1. RE-GROUND AFTER EVERY EDIT. Every apply mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — take the next edit's numbers from the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`. Stale tag or surprise? STOP, re-`read`.
2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.
</critical>

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the working directory; returns stdout and stderr, truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB. Timeouts you set are retried automatically (3 attempts total) as [bash attempt N]; environment-default timeouts fail once with the partial output. For long-running commands (builds, servers, watchers) pass background: true — you get the job id immediately and a notice when it finishes; check progress with bash_job. A foreground command still running when the user sends a message is moved to a background job untouched (never killed). A command still running after 60s is moved to a background job automatically (never restarted); carried timeouts are NOT auto-retried — retry if the completion notice reports a timeout.

tools.name: bash_job
tools.description: Manage background shell jobs (from bash background: true). Actions: "status" lists running + last 20 exited (all: true = every job; id = one), "output" tails a log (id, lines), "stop" kills a running job (id).

tools.name: lsp
tools.description:
Query a language server for diagnostics, navigation, and renames. For Dart/Flutter workspaces the Dart analysis server (`dart language-server`) starts automatically on first use; other servers can be added via `.fah/lsp.json`.

## Ops

- `diagnostics {path}` — analyzer errors/warnings for a file. Returns `OK` when clean.
- `definition {path, line, character}` — where the symbol at the position is defined.
- `references {path, line, character}` — every reference to the symbol at the position.
- `rename {path, line, character, newName}` — rename the symbol at the position workspace-wide. The server's workspace edit is applied atomically, so barrel files and imports update together; per-file edit counts are reported.

`line` and `character` are 1-indexed and default to 1.

## Rules

- Prefer this over `bash dart analyze` for a single file; diagnostics come back scoped and severity-sorted.
- Prefer `rename` over manual search-and-replace for identifiers: the analysis server finds every reference, including exports and imports.
- Positions point at the symbol's first letter. When unsure of the exact column, `read` the line first.
- Definition/references results render as `file:line:col` with the source line; follow up with `read` for more context.
- If no server is configured for a file type, add one to `.fah/lsp.json` (servers map with `command`, `args`, `fileTypes`, `rootMarkers`).

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web and return ranked results with [n] citation markers, titles, URLs, and snippets. Runs a provider chain (DuckDuckGo first, keyed providers when configured) and falls through on failure. Follow up with web_fetch on a result URL to read the full page.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return its main content as Markdown: headings, link anchors, lists, and code blocks are preserved, navigation and boilerplate are stripped. Known sites (pub.dev) are rendered via dedicated handlers. Use it to read pages found with web_search.

tools.name: config
tools.description: Inspect and edit the fa configuration — the user file ~/.fah/config.yaml and the project .fah/config.yaml — without a shell (the same core the `fa config` CLI verbs wrap, available on every host). ops: check = validate both files with the real parsers (errors/warnings/notes + a final ok/failed line); path = list the config file locations and whether each exists; get = the effective value of a dotted key (project scope wins where it participates); set = a surgical single-key write that validates the edited file BEFORE writing, so an invalid value persists nothing. Config keys are documented in the fa-self-config skill — never invent one; unknown keys are rejected. A set result names the file, scope, old -> new value, and whether the change applies live or at next boot.

tools.name: memory_add
tools.description:
# `memory_add` policy

## What to store

Store only **durable** facts — things that must survive across sessions:

- project conventions, architecture decisions and their rationale;
- user preferences, habits, environment facts;
- key discoveries that were expensive to learn (non-obvious behaviour,
  gotchas, working configurations).

Do **not** store task progress, transient state, or anything derivable
from the repository itself (file contents, git history, current diffs).

## The supersede rule

Facts age. When a problem is **solved** or a fact **changes**:

1. delete the outdated record (`memory_delete` by id or exact text —
   deletions are tombstoned, so the old text cannot be re-captured);
2. add the new fact as a fresh record.

Never leave temporary difficulties, workarounds, or "currently broken"
notes in memory forever. A memory full of solved problems actively
misleads future sessions. If you used a record to fix something, that
record's job is done — supersede it.

Before adding anything, `memory_search` for an existing record on the
topic: update (delete + add) instead of duplicating.

## Scope discipline

- **project scope** (default) lives in the project's memory directory and
  is **public**: it is committed to git and shared with everyone who
  clones the repository. Never store secrets, credentials, personal data,
  or anything you would not put in a public commit message.
- **user scope** is global and private to the user's machine. Use it for
  cross-project preferences and facts about the user.

## Style

- One fact per record, concise and self-contained (readable without the
  conversation that produced it).
- Add concrete tags (see [tag_taxonomy.md](tag_taxonomy.md)).
- Prefer facts with staying power: "tests run with `--exclude-tags
  integration`" outlives "I am currently fixing the test suite".

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search long-term memory for relevant facts, preferences, or past decisions. Use proactively before tasks that might benefit from prior context.

tools.name: memory_list
tools.description: List recent long-term memory entries. Useful to review what the agent already knows.

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.description: Delete a stale, wrong, or obsolete entry from long-term memory by id. Prefer deleting over rewriting when the fact no longer holds at all.

tools.name: schedule_message
tools.description: Send a delayed message to an agent mailbox (your own by default) — schedule a follow-up task to check on something later. The message wakes the recipient when it fires; it survives restarts.

tools.name: ask
tools.description:
Ask the user one or more structured questions when you need clarification or a decision during task execution.

<conditions>
- Multiple approaches exist with significantly different tradeoffs the user should weigh
</conditions>

<instruction>
- Use `questions` for multiple related questions instead of asking one at a time
- Use `recommended` (0-based option index or exact option label) to mark the default; the UI badges it as "Recommended"
- Set `multiSelect: true` on a question to allow multiple selections
- Use short option labels; put explanatory tradeoffs in an option's `description` instead of merging them into the label
- Omit `options` when the answer is free-form text
</instruction>

<caution>
- Provide 2-5 concise, distinct options per question
</caution>

<critical>
- **Default to action.** Resolve ambiguity yourself using repo conventions, existing patterns, and reasonable defaults. Exhaust existing sources (code, configs, docs, history) before asking. Only ask when options have materially different tradeoffs the user must decide.
- **If multiple choices are acceptable**, pick the most conservative/standard option and proceed; state the choice.
- **Do NOT include an "Other" option** — the UI always offers free-text input alongside your options.
</critical>

tools.name: request_secret
tools.description:
Ask the user for a credential (API key, token, password) that you need and that is not available yet.

<conditions>
- A command or call fails because a credential is missing, or the task clearly requires one
- The secret is NOT already in the "Available secret env vars" list
</conditions>

<instruction>
- Set `name` to the conventional env var name for the service (GITHUB_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, NPM_TOKEN...); the user can adjust it before saving
- Explain in `reason` what you need the credential for — the user sees this text
- After the user saves it, reference it as $NAME in shell commands; the value itself never enters the conversation
</instruction>

<critical>
- NEVER ask the user to paste a secret into the chat as plain text — always use this tool, so the value is stored securely and redacted from the transcript
- NEVER print, echo, or write the secret value after it is saved
- If the user declines, do not immediately retry the same request; find another way or explain the blocker
</critical>

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generates an image from a text prompt. Requires the imageGeneration slot to be configured (models.slots.imageGeneration in ~/.fah/config.yaml, or useMainConnection: true to opt into the main connection explicitly). Returns a path to the saved image file. Arguments: prompt (required), size (optional, e.g. "1024x1024"), quality (optional), images (optional, list of reference images: sandbox paths, http(s) URLs, or base64 — supported by OpenRouter image endpoints that accept image input).

tools.name: generate_video
tools.description: Generates a video from a text prompt. Requires the videoGeneration slot to be configured (models.slots.videoGeneration in ~/.fah/config.yaml, or useMainConnection: true to opt into the main connection explicitly). Returns a path to the saved MP4 file. Arguments: prompt (required), size (optional, e.g. "1920x1080"), quality (optional), images (optional, list of reference images: sandbox paths, http(s) URLs, or base64 — supported by OpenRouter video endpoints that accept image input).

tools.name: decide
tools.description: Ask a structured decision model (OpenRouter Decisions API, e.g. inception/mercury-decide:free) typed questions about a state and receive calibrated answers as structured JSON: yes-no questions come back with a probability, choice questions with the picked option plus per-option probabilities, score questions with a calibrated score over the ordered legend. Requires the main connection to be an OpenRouter provider. Arguments: model (required), state (required — text or JSON), questions (required — object keyed by question name; each entry is {type: bool|choice|score, instructions, criteria} — bool questions ride the Decisions API's `noul` wire type)

tools.name: task_status
tools.description: Check the status of spawned subagents. Without an id, lists ALL subagents with their current state, token usage, and last activity. With an id, shows that subagent in detail.

tools.name: task_observe
tools.description: Read the recent message history of a subagent. Useful to inspect what a child discovered or decided before following up.

tools.name: task_send
tools.description: Send a follow-up message to a subagent. A running child receives it in its inbox at the next turn boundary; an idle (waiting for input) or completed child is resumed in its SAME session with the message. The resume wait is capped (1.5s): a child that does not respond in time reports the message queued and keeps waking in the background (check task_status). Failed children are continued with task_resume instead. Remote a2a:<name> children cannot be steered or resumed — they have no local session or inbox; follow up with a new task item.

tools.name: task_resume
tools.description: Resume a FAILED subagent, continuing the SAME session: the run appends to the existing JSONL transcript, keeps the same mailbox id and display name, and never mints a cloned "name-2" session. Use this after transient failures (provider quota, network). The resume wait is capped (1.5s): a child that does not confirm in time reports the resume continuing in the background — it is never restarted (check task_status). Steering running/idle/completed children is task_send; respawning a fresh agent is task (the new child links supersedes).

tools.name: task_cancel
tools.description: Abort a running background subagent job by id (see task_status for ids). The child agent is cancelled; already-settled jobs report their state instead.

tools.name: reply
tools.description:
Deliver your explicit answer to the parent agent. Call this when your task output is ready — the text becomes the parent-visible reply. If you never call it, the parent still sees your final message as a completion notice, but an explicit reply is the reliable channel.

REPORT SIZE: per-message budget 8000 chars — you may send one complete reply even when it is larger: the harness auto-spills it (the full text is stored as an agent:// artifact; the parent gets an excerpt + pointer + completeness, and this tool result names the reference). Manual chunking (ordered agent_message parts with report_id + 0-based part_index, more=false on the last, then a final manifest reply carrying report_id + report_parts) is the FALLBACK for when auto-spill is unavailable. See REPORT SIZE CONTRACT in your system prompt. Never probe the output limit.

tools.name: agent_message
tools.description:
Send a message to another agent: a SIBLING subagent id, "main" for the parent orchestrator (for a final answer prefer reply), an absolute mailbox "<sessionId>/main" to reach another Fa instance sharing this session repo, or "name@machine" to reach a session on another machine (delivered through the A2A gateway; the remote machine must be configured under a2a.servers). A session display NAME from agent_directory works too: "goal_builder" or "goal_builder/main" resolve to that session's live mailbox. The recipient sees the message in its inbox on its next turn; completed siblings are resumed. Unknown ids and full queues are rejected.

REPORT SIZE: budget 8000 chars — oversized same-session bodies auto-spill (stored as an agent:// artifact and delivered as a bounded envelope). Manual chunking (ordered report_id + part_index parts) is the FALLBACK for when auto-spill is unavailable. See REPORT SIZE CONTRACT in your system prompt.

tools.name: agent_directory
tools.description: List the agent mailboxes in the messaging fabric that are worth talking to: LIVE mailboxes (registration-backed presence or recent activity), any mailbox holding pending mail, your subagents, and your own address (marked). Each entry shows its session display NAME when known, a short mailbox id, the pending message count, presence ("live" / "busy (run in progress, accepts mail)" / "offline"), the last-activity time for offline entries, and the working directory (home shortened to ~). Declared capabilities render as sub-lines. Stale mailboxes are hidden — pass all: true to list those too (that also shows FULL mailbox ids; the default view truncates them to save tokens). Address a mailbox by its session name via agent_message ("goal_builder", "goal_builder/main", or "name@machine" — a peer on another machine is reachable through the A2A gateway when an a2a.servers entry exists for it); asleep targets are woken with a headless run automatically.

tools.name: task
tools.description:
Your session context is limited. Before performing a user request, think whether the work can be delegated to subagents — orchestrate subagents and deliver the result to the user. If it is a simple ask, just perform it yourself.

Run subagents in parallel by passing multiple items in a single `tasks[]` batch. Execution blocks until every item finishes unless `background` is true — then you receive job ids immediately and results deliver as jobs settle.

# Task Design
- **Agent typing:** Pick each item's `agent` type. Read-only research MUST use `agent: "explore"`. Use the default worker only when no specialist fits.
- **No overhead:** Each `task` MUST instruct its subagent to skip formatters, linters, and project-wide test suites. Run those once at the end.
- **One pass:** Prefer subagents that investigate AND edit in one pass; spin a read-only `explore` only when the affected files are genuinely unknown.

# Inputs
- `context`: Shared project state, constraints, and contracts. Applies to the entire batch; do not duplicate this background into individual tasks.
- `tasks[]`: Array of subagents to spawn.
  - `name`: A stable identifier (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`), used to address the agent (`agent://` urls, job ids). Uniquified per session; generated from the agent type if omitted.
  - `agent`: The agent type running this item. Omitting it gives you the general-purpose worker (`task`) — NEVER pass that name explicitly. Only omit it after checking the agent list below and finding no specialist that fits.
  - `task`: Complete, self-contained instructions. One-liners or missing acceptance criteria are PROHIBITED.
  - `outputSchema`: Invocation-specific JSON Schema. The subagent's final message must then be a JSON document satisfying it; invalid output gets ONE fix retry, then the item fails.
- `background`: Run items as background jobs (default: host configuration). Blocking calls return every item's output in the result.

# Communication
Subagents start blank — no conversation history. Put everything they need into `context` (shared) and `task` (per item). After spawn, the family stays connected:
- `task_send {id, message}`: steer a running child, answer a waiting (idle) one, or RESUME a completed one with follow-up work.
- `task_resume {id, message?}`: continue a FAILED child in its SAME session — same id, same transcript, same mailbox, never a cloned `name-2` session. Use it after transient failures (provider quota, network); `task_send` is for running/idle/completed children, a fresh `task` for a clean restart (the new child links `supersedes`).
- `task_status` / `task_observe`: inspect the family at any time — status, tokens, and the child's recent transcript.
- Children can `reply` (their explicit answer to you) and `agent_message` (sibling↔sibling hand-offs) — a child that finishes without replying surfaces a `completed_without_reply` notice with its final text preview.
- Completed subagents stay addressable: send them more work instead of re-spawning duplicates.
- Remote `a2a:<name>` children cannot be steered, resumed, or observed — they have no local session. Follow up with a new task item against the same `a2a:<name>` agent.

# Waiting is idle, not blocked
- Long-running children (test suites, builds, research): spawn them with `background: true` and END YOUR TURN right after spawning. Completions and inbox mail wake you automatically, and each result arrives as a message — waiting is an idle state, never a blocked turn.
- NEVER park your turn waiting on children (foreground watch loops, blocking re-polls, sleep-style watchers). A parked turn is unreachable: owner messages queue behind it for as long as the wedge lasts.
- If a blocking call is still running when a user message arrives, the call soft-yields to background — do not re-block afterwards; finish the reply and end the turn.

# Format Contracts
`context` format:
# Goal         ← what the batch accomplishes
# Constraints  ← rules and session decisions
# Contract     ← shared interfaces

`task` format:
# Target       ← exact files and symbols; explicit non-goals
# Change       ← step-by-step add/remove/rename; APIs and patterns
# Acceptance   ← observable result; no project-wide commands

# Results
Each item's full output is addressable as `agent://<id>`. An explicit child `reply` is the deliverable — verbatim within the budget, else a bounded `agent://` envelope (excerpt + pointer + completeness); never a silent stub. Resumed children carry their final answer on the completion notice; a reply acked before a kill survives the resume. For items with an `outputSchema`, the stored output IS the validated JSON object, so typed fields are addressable as `agent://<id>/<dot.path>` (e.g. `agent://Explore/findings.0.path`).

# Report Size
A child report above the per-message budget is never silently truncated: the full redacted text is stored as an `agent://` artifact and the result carries a bounded excerpt, the pointer, and explicit completeness (`complete`/`partial`). Resolve the pointer for the whole report. Chunked reports get a final manifest `reply` the harness validates against the observed parts; missing, duplicated, or out-of-order sets are marked INCOMPLETE.

# Available Agents
### task
General-purpose subagent with full capabilities for delegated multi-step tasks
### explore (READ-ONLY)
Read-only codebase research: rapid analysis, pattern searches, and compressed findings for handoff (uses the smol model role when configured)
### review (READ-ONLY)
Read-only code review specialist for quality and security analysis (uses the slow model role when configured)
### plan (READ-ONLY)
Read-only planning specialist that produces implementation plans without editing code

tools.name: checkpoint
tools.description:
Creates a context checkpoint before exploratory work so you can later rewind and keep only a concise report.

Use this when you need to investigate with many intermediate tool calls (read/grep/glob/etc.) and want to minimize context cost afterward.

Rules:
- You MUST call `rewind` before finishing after starting a checkpoint.
- You NEVER call `checkpoint` while another checkpoint is active in the
  same turn. A checkpoint never spans user turns: if one is left unrewound
  when the turn ends, the next `checkpoint` call auto-closes it (the tool
  result names the closed checkpoint) and proceeds.

Typical flow:
1. `checkpoint(goal: …)`
2. Perform exploratory work
3. `rewind(report: …)` with concise findings

After rewind, intermediate checkpoint messages are removed from active context and replaced by the report. The dropped history stays in the session tree; nothing is lost.

tools.name: rewind
tools.description:
End an active checkpoint. Rewind context to it, replacing intermediate exploration with your report.

Call immediately after `checkpoint`-started investigative work.

Requirements:
- `report` MUST be concise, factual, and actionable.
- Include key findings, decisions, and any unresolved risks.
- AVOID raw scratch logs unless essential.
- You MUST call this before finishing if a checkpoint is active.

Behavior:
- If no checkpoint is active, this tool errors. If the checkpoint already rewound, continue from the retained report instead of retrying.
- On success, the session rewinds, keeps your report as retained context, and closes the checkpoint.
- A successful rewind is final for that checkpoint; repeat calls error.

tools.name: compact_expand
tools.description:
Surface and reopen hidden context segments.

Call with NO arguments to list what is hidden: the index of hidden segments with id, kind, size, and a first-line preview each. Pass `query` to filter and rank that index by keyword — it searches the full hidden content, not just previews, so use it when you know WHAT you need but not the id. Discovery is free: it never consumes the expand budget.

To read a segment back, pass its numeric id or range from a marker as `target` (e.g. `5` or `2-6`). Context markers like `[3:hidden·tool_result·4.2k·"first line…"]` or `[2-6:ckpt·38k→40tok·covers:3,5]` are doors, not gravestones: the underlying records stay on disk.

- Giant segments are paged: pass `page` (1-based) to continue past the first page; each page footer states the exact continue call.
- Expanded content counts toward a per-turn budget; every success states the budget left, and when the budget is exhausted the result says so and resets on the next user turn. Only hidden, checkpoint-covered, or summary-folded records expand — the tool tells you when a record is already visible.
- The session file never changes; an expanded segment may be re-hidden later by compaction.

Prefer a targeted expand over re-reading files when the fact was already in context once, and prefer discovery + query over blind ids.

## Managing segments yourself (tier 2)

Pass `action` with a `target` to manage segments directly, without waiting for pressure:

- `action: "hide"` folds a segment you know is dead weight into its expandable marker immediately — one-line marker stays where the content was, `compact_expand` reopens it any time. Real user turns are never hideable; pair groups hide whole; the most recent turns and pinned segments are rejected with the reason.
- `action: "pin"` shields a segment from every hide/compact path (yours, the judge's, pressure-time LRU re-hide); `action: "unpin"` releases it. Pins render on the marker (`·pinned`) and survive session reload.

Hiding and pinning are session state, not edits: the records stay in the file byte-for-byte.

tools.name: session_search
tools.description: Search the WHOLE session archive (every past turn — hidden, compacted and checkpointed regions included), not just the current context. Use it whenever the user references a past decision, rule, task or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made") BEFORE answering from assumption. Returns pointers (id, kind, timestamp, preview), never full content — pull the record back with compact_expand. With mode: "map" it reports the archive structure instead: record-kind counts, hidden/checkpoint totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth.

 * Defense-in-depth guard: the agent is instructed (instructions/pr_review/output_rules.md,

/**
 * The one model-written-path guard (gh-1350 class): a file reference from
 * the review model is only trusted in the comment-file layout — a bare

 * every write of a model-written file reference goes through this shape

 * unguarded — a hallucinated path could append the stamp to any readable
 * file relative to the runtime cwd, e.g. a repo source file).
 */
function isCommentFilePath(value) {

        /^(outputs\/)?(pr_review_comments\/)?[\w.\-]+\.md$/.test(value.trim());

**Fixed.** The demote-note delivery is now shape-aware — both tolerated input shapes get the provenance note without corrupting the posted thread.

- **Shape A (body-as-path hybrid)**: `stampDemotionBody` (`js/common/reviewFilter.js`) no longer appends to a body that passes the path-shape guard — appending would break `resolveInlineComment`'s resolution and the poster would publish the literal path + note. Instead the wired runner stamps the referenced file: `stampOneDemotion` (`js/postPRReviewComments.js`) now targets `entry.comment` **or**, when the comment field is absent, the path-shaped `entry.body` — the poster keeps resolving the untouched body to the file content, which now carries the note. Pinned by "applyReviewFilter — a body-as-path hybrid gets its note in the FILE, body stays resolvable (round 2, shape A)" (asserts `body === path` after the demote, `isCommentFilePath(body)` still true, and the note inside the file) and at the pure layer by "stampDemotionBody leaves a body-as-path hybrid untouched" — both RED-verified against the pre-fix code.
- **Shape B (old-spec `{file, comment}`)**: `isStampTarget` now matches `(entry.path || entry.file)` against the stamp's path, so an old-spec entry's comment file receives the note exactly like agent-output entries (the structured tier still downgrades the same way). Pinned by "applyReviewFilter — old-spec {file, comment} gets the note in its comment file (round 2, shape B)" — RED-verified (pre-fix: severity downgraded, file untouched).
- The path-shape guard itself now has a single owner: `isCommentFilePath` moved to the pure `js/common/reviewFilter.js` (exported; `postPRReviewComments.js` aliases it), so the pure apply and the wired runner test the same predicate — no drift.

2. **💡 Docs trial opt-in phasing** — now states the opt-in lands in the follow-up config change post-merge (knob ships blockless), matching the config comment; generated copy regenerated.
3. **🪶 Prose-strip trade-off** — accepted per the finding's suggested disposition and pinned with the control test asserting both reproductions (test-only).
4. **🪶 Eager diff-path probes** — `filterDiffPathOf` now evaluated only when `verificationEnabledOf(ctx.reviewPolicy)`; a `none` round runs zero `pr_diff.txt` probes (pinned by a file-read-counting action test).
